items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: And if you notice, on my chorus, I play some of his licks. Not many of his exact licks. In other words, I play, I phrase the way he would have phrased it.

ctx.x: Now, the reason why I like this book, I've never heard Louis Armstrong play it. But I can always hear him with my mind's ear playing this. Because it sounds like he should have played this number. And if you notice, on my chorus, I play some of his licks. Not many of his exact licks. In other words, I play, I phrase the way he would have phrased it. On spots. Not all the way through my solo. But some spots on my solo I phrase it. Was he any good? Oh, Louis Armstrong? Yes, he did. He said the style, he said the…
You don't think he was just a clown?

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: I just stood up in front of the bandstand just looking at him, just looking at him playing the trumpet.

ctx.x: What do you remember about that night when you saw Louis?
I didn't dance, I had my girlfriend with me. And I didn't dance at all, it was a dance. I just stood up in front of the bandstand just looking at him, just looking at him playing the trumpet.
Did you try to watch his fingering?
